---
title: Porting from pkucli
description: pkucli is the protocol reference for PKU services. How to port endpoints, login steps and quirks from its Rust crates into a plugin, leave sign-in to the app, and credit the source file.
icon: Terminal
---

[`pkuinfo/pkucli`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pkucli) is a set of command-line tools for PKU web
services, written in Rust. Its authors have already worked out the hard parts of each service:
which endpoints exist, which sign-in steps the service needs, which headers and parameters it
requires, and how its HTML is structured.

When you write a plugin for a service that pkucli already supports, port pkucli's behaviour instead
of working it out again, and cite the source file in a comment. This page shows where to find things
in pkucli, which parts belong in the plugin and which stay in the app, and an example.

Most services sign in through IAAA, PKU's central sign-in system (iaaa.pku.edu.cn). After IAAA,
each service usually needs one or more single sign-on (SSO) steps of its own. We call each such step
a _login hop_.

## Where things are

| pkucli crate | Service | In PKU Harness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `common` | IAAA login (password, QR code), TOTP codes, captcha, sessions, credentials | The app (`src/core/campus`); **not** in plugins |
| `campuscard` | Campus card (bdcard) | `wallet` plugin, `card` campus service |
| `treehole` | Treehole (树洞) | `treehole` plugin, `treehole` service |
| `course` | Blackboard (教学网) | `courses` plugin, `blackboard` service |
| `elective` | Course selection | `elective` plugin, `elective` service |
| `cwfw`, `cwpay` | Finance, finance payments | `finance` plugin, `cwfw` / `cwpay` services |
| `bdkj` | Room booking | `room-booking` plugin, `bdkj` service |
| `portal` | Portal | The portal's SSO hop, inside the app |
| `claspider` | Course recordings (智云课堂) | Planned |
| `info-spider`, `info-auth` | WeChat articles | `notices` plugin reads single articles (cleaning ported from `info-spider`) |

TOTP (time-based one-time password) is the six-digit code an authenticator app shows. Inside a
crate, `api.rs` (or `client.rs`) holds the endpoints and response types, `login.rs` holds the
service's own login hops, and `commands.rs` holds the operations a user runs.

## What moves where

Each file of a pkucli crate maps to a place in PKU Harness. Sign-in moves into the app, and
everything else moves into the plugin:

```
pkucli crate                     PKU Harness
─────────────────────────────    ──────────────────────────────────────────────
login.rs  (IAAA → service SSO)   app: a campus service adapter (harness-owned)
client.rs (headers, base URL)    plugin: the `url`/`headers` of services.campus.request
api.rs    (endpoints, types)     plugin: src/api.ts + zod/TS types
commands.rs / display.rs         plugin: tools (data, not formatted text)
```

- **Sign-in stays in the app.** A plugin never implements IAAA or a service's SSO hops, so it never
  handles a password. Today the app signs in to `card`, `its`, `treehole`, `blackboard`, `bdkj`,
  `cwfw`, `cwpay`, `elective`, `library` and `library-space`. If the service you need is not in that
  list, open an issue in `pku-harness`. A new service needs a new adapter in
  `src/core/campus/adapters/`.
- **Requests go through `services.campus.request(service, req)`.** Give paths relative to the
  service's host. The app adds the cookies or tokens.
- **Public pages** that need no login can use plain `fetch` with `requires: ['network']`. Copy
  pkucli's headers, such as a desktop user agent and `accept-language: zh-CN`, because some campus
  servers reject requests without them.
- **Parse into data.** pkucli's `display.rs` formats output for a terminal. A tool returns structured
  JSON instead, because its reader is the model or a screen.

## Example

Here is the campus card query in pkucli, written in Rust:

```rust title="crates/campuscard/src/api.rs"
/// 查询校园卡信息
pub async fn query_card(&self) -> Result<CardQueryData> {
    let url = format!("{CARD_BASE}/berserker-app/ykt/tsm/queryCard?synAccessSource=h5");
    let resp = self.http.get(&url).send().await.context("查询校园卡失败")?;
    let api_resp: ApiResp<CardQueryData> = parse_response(resp).await?;
    check_resp(api_resp)
}
```

The same request in a plugin, written in TypeScript. The comment at the top credits the pkucli file
and records two quirks: amounts are in fen (0.01 yuan), and every call carries
`synAccessSource=h5`.

```ts title="plugins/shared/campus-card.ts (abridged)"
/**
 * Campus card (bdcard.pku.edu.cn) response handling, ported from pkucli
 * crates/campuscard/src/api.rs. Amounts are in fen; every call carries synAccessSource=h5.
 */
import type { HostServices } from '@pku-harness/sdk';

type Services = Pick<HostServices, 'campus'>;
const get = (services: Services, url: string) => services.campus.request('card', { url });

export async function cardAccount(services: Services) {
  const data = unwrap<{ card: CardInfo[] }>(await get(services, '/berserker-app/ykt/tsm/queryCard?synAccessSource=h5'));
  const account = data.card[0]?.account;
  if (!account) throw new Error('校园卡缺少账户信息');
  return account;
}
```

## Second factors

Some services ask for an extra check, such as an SMS code. pkucli asks for the code in the
terminal, which a plugin can't do. In a plugin, a check at the service level becomes a tool result
such as `{ status: 'verification_required', methods: ['sms'], message }`, together with a tool that
sends or redeems the code. Treehole's SMS check (error `40002`) and its course token (error `40077`)
work this way. The plugin's screen can also offer `services.sms.awaitCode()`, which reads the code
from the SMS.

Second factors at the IAAA level are handled by the app, not by plugins.

## Rules

- **MUST** cite the pkucli file you ported from in a comment at the top of the module.
- **MUST** keep sign-in in the app. Plugins only make requests.
- **SHOULD** port each parser together with a test and a fixture made from a real, anonymised
  response.
- **SHOULD** fix bugs in both places. If you find a quirk pkucli doesn't handle, open an issue or a
  pull request in pkucli too.
